course_description:
This course will support people currently working in health care systems or who seek careers in health care systems to engage effectively with digital health in practice for the benefit of patients. Students will gain an understanding and appreciation of clinical governance, ethics and information management as well as the practical aspects of introducing and working with new technology in different working environments.

This course will assist students to develop skills in selecting and implementing digital health technologies to address real-world challenges. Students will explore different aspects of digital health implementation including identifying barriers to adopting new technology; developing problem statements; clinical governance, privacy, and ethics; communication strategies; and using digital health and clinical informatics to advance the provision of evidence-based care. Students will also learn about the procurement process within a healthcare setting and how to prepare a healthcare budget in the context of digital health implementation.

Over the 13-week online program, students will develop a coherent understanding of clinical, business, and technological terminologies and processes required to implement digital health in various healthcare systems. Students will also learn from industry-leading champions on existing digital health projects and how to successfully navigate the diverse healthcare landscape. In the conclusion of this course, students will prepare a digital health implementation plan of a technology to address a self-selected challenge in a real-world health context.

AI tools may be used to support learning and task completion in this course, and the course provides guidance on appropriate use. Students are expected to apply judgement when using these tools, to check outputs carefully, and to ensure that all submitted work reflects their own understanding. Students are responsible for ensuring that any use of AI complies with academic integrity requirements and is appropriately acknowledged.

course_aims: The objective of this course aims to empower students to design and create a digital health implementation plan to deliver high-quality, accessible and efficient healthcare solutions in contemporary health settings.

learning_outcomes.description: Use an ethical, evidence-based, and clinically governed approach to select a digital health intervention in various settings.
Analyse the stakeholder perspectives, barriers, and facilitators of digital health interventions on local and organisational levels
Lead an evidence-based digital health intervention specific to your own context
Evaluate the clinical, business, and technological processes of various digital health initiatives and settings

assessment_details.title: Annotated Bibliography and Synthesis
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment starts the process of you designing an implementation plan for a digital health intervention in a healthcare setting of your choice. You will demonstrate your understanding of the challenges faced by the existing healthcare setting and how digital health can address these challenges. Individually, you will create: a 100-word introduction outlining the healthcare setting of your choice and the planned digital health intervention; a 10-item annotated bibliography; a 300-word synthesis of the evidence (from the 10 studies selected previously) and problem statement. Your problem statement will define a challenge faced by the healthcare setting that can be addressed by your digital health intervention. Discuss why this problem needs to be addressed and how it will advance the Quintuple aim of healthcare. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Project Management Plan for Implementation
assessment_details.task_description: You are to work individually to prepare a Project Management and Plan for Implementation (PMPI). A PMPI is a multiple page document that clearly outlines the implementation strategy. The report includes written sections that outline various strategies and summaries of assessments that have been/will be undertaken. Part 1 of the assessment covers topics discussed in the first part of the course including implementation framework, governance, privacy and ethical considerations, and user-centred design. Part 2 of the assessment covers topics discussed in the second part of the course including stakeholder engagement, budget and procurement, and monitoring and evaluation plan. You are strongly encouraged to continue with the digital health intervention submitted for assessment from earlier in the course. Changes to the digital health intervention and healthcare setting can be discussed with the course coordinator on an individual basis. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Digital health intervention pitch
assessment_details.due_date: 30/10/2026 4:00 pm Presentation completed live online. Following your presentation, you will be asked to join a breakout room and show your ID (e.g. student ID, driver's license, passport) for identity verification purposes. The pitch will be held between 4pm-6pm.
assessment_details.task_description: Throughout this course, you have been developing the knowledge and skills to implement a digital health intervention in a healthcare service. This assessment is an opportunity for you to apply your understanding of the course content to a setting specific to you in an oral pitch. In this task, you are pitching to the operational unit where your digital health implementation will theoretically take place. For example, if you are introducing an ieMR dashboard for patients undergoing lung transplant, your operational unit would likely be the clinician’s part of the transplant team. Ensure that your presentation is targeted and addresses the specific needs for your audience. You are to work individually to prepare an 8-minute oral pitch that builds on your existing knowledge and research from your previous assessments. Your presentation will be followed by a question-and-answer session and identity verification. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. In accordance with UQ Assessment Policy, your presentation will be recorded.
